channel.title: Security-announce
channel.description: Mailing list for security advisories affecting Python or pip

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-107784] tarfile extraction filters accept drive-relative paths on Windows
item.description:
There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
On Windows, the tarfile "tar" and "data" extraction filters did not reject member names or link targets that have a drive but no root, such as "C:foo". When extracting to a relative destination, such a member was written to the current working directory of that drive instead of the destination, and a symbolic link with such a target pointed outside the destination. The filters now refuse these member names and link targets with AbsolutePathError and AbsoluteLinkError.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-107784 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/161334
item.author: stanulbrych＠gmail.com (Stan Ulbrych)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-133949] pip bundles compromised eMudhra certificates via certifi
item.description:
There is a CRITICAL severity vulnerability affecting pip.
pip prior to v26.2.2 the certifi bundled with pip contains the compromised eMudhra certificates.
Upgrading to a secure version of pip should be done either by first upgrading Python to a version that rejects the compromised intermediates ( https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-115557) or use hash pinning with a known-secure version of pip.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://github.com/advisories/ghsa-6q48-6c7w-9gw2 * https://discuss.python.org/t/information-for-python-users-regarding-emudhra-emsign-ca-certificate-security-incident/109576 * https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-133949 * https://github.com/pypa/pip/pull/14371
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-16052] Cookie Attribute Injection via Unescaped Semicolons in http.cookies.Morsel
item.description:
There is a LOW severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
The http.cookies.Morsel class allows separator semicolons in attribute values and includes them verbatim in all output formats. An attacker who can control these values could use this to relax the cookie's Domain or SameSite restrictions.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-16052 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/161711
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-115559] imaplib STARTTLS serves plaintext bytes buffered before the handshake as if they came over TLS
item.description:
There is a medium severity vulnerability affecting the imaplib library in CPython.
IMAP4.starttls() wraps the socket in TLS but leaves self._readbuf, imaplib's own read-ahead buffer, untouched. Any plaintext bytes that arrived in the same recv() as the tagged OK to STARTTLS are returned by readline() after the handshake, so the client treats them as the first responses on the protected channel. A network attacker who cannot break TLS can append forged lines after the server's OK, let the handshake complete with the real server and a valid certificate, and have the client accept the forged CAPABILITY and the forged tagged completion of the next command. This is the STARTTLS command/response injection class of CVE-2011-0411.
First affected release: 3.14.0. The regression comes from the IMAP4 IDLE support in gh-55454 (commit 0fef47e), which replaced self._file.readline() with the custom _readbuf buffering. Before that, starttls() replaced the file object and so discarded buffered plaintext; 3.13.13 is not affected.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-115559 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/160370
Thanks to ＠digit50 for reporting this issue.
item.author: jelle.zijlstra＠gmail.com (Jelle Zijlstra)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-115791] Prevent shadowing stdlib in gzip/tarfile/zipfile CLI
item.description:
There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
When tarfile or zipfile command line interface (CLI) is used to decompress an archive, a Python script shadowing the stdlib can be created. Then if an error occurs during decompressing the next file, the newly created Python script is executed. This is especially true if the created Python is called traceback.py. The problem is that Python adds the current directory to sys.path when python -m MODULE is run, and the archive is also decompressed in the current directory.
The fix removes sys.path[0] in gzip, tarfile and zipfile command line interface to prevent shadowing standard library modules from extracted files.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-115791 * https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/161705
item.author: vstinner＠python.org (Victor Stinner)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-19552] ssl.get_server_certificate(addr, ca_certs=...) verifies the chain but never the identity
item.description:
There is a LOW severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
When ca_certs parameter was supplied to ssl.get_server_certificate() function, the identity of the certificate is not checked.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-19552 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/161507
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-124249] http.cookiejar deletes cookies of other domains via expired Set-Cookie
item.description:
There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
http.cookiejar.CookieJar deleted a stored cookie when a response carried an already expired Set-Cookie header for it, using the Domain and Path attributes from the header without consulting the cookie policy. A server could therefore delete cookies belonging to other domains from a shared cookie jar, such as the one used by urllib's HTTPCookieProcessor. The fix consults the cookie policy before an expired cookie may delete an existing one, as required by RFC 6265 section 5.3.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-124249 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/161570
item.author: kirill.bast＠gmail.com (Kirill Podoprigora)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-119170] Regression in FIPS enforcement of hash algorithms affecting only Python 3.14.10
item.description:
There is a HIGH severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
There was a regression in how FIPS algorithms were enforced for the hashlib module. Only users that are using OpenSSL in FIPS mode are affected. Only Python 3.14.10 is affected, all other Python versions are unaffected.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-119170 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/160984
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.description:

socket.getaddrinfo() previously accepted null bytes within *host* and *port* parameters which can cause the values to be silently truncated.

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-103995] Lenient parsing of integers for response body and chunk framing
item.description:

Response body and chunk parsing would handle non-hex or negative integers incorrectly which could result in misinterpreting HTTP response contents.

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-115557] Distrust compromised intermediate certificates in ssl module
item.description:
Python has added a denylist for known compromised certificates to the "ssl" module to ensure user safety even without certificate revocation configured. Known compromised certificates on this denylist will automatically be rejected regardless of the SSLContext policy configuration.
Please see the linked CVE ID for more information:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-115557 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/160042
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-114583] tarfile.tar_filter path traversal bypass allows writing outside the extraction directory
item.description:
There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
tarfile.tar_filter could be bypassed using crafted link entries, including symlinks with empty or directory-like names, to redirect later archive members outside the intended extraction directory. This allowed a malicious tar archive to cause tarfile.extractall() with filter="tar" to write files outside the destination directory, subject to the permissions of the extracting process.
This is the tarfile.tar_filter counterpart of CVE-2026-7774, which covered tarfile.data_filter.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-114583 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/160098
item.author: stanulbrych＠gmail.com (Stan Ulbrych)

item.title: [Security-announce][GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2] CRITICAL security update for certifi, removal of emSign root certificate
item.description:
There is a CRITICAL severity vulnerability affecting certifi.
Certifi 2026.10.19 removes root certificates from "emSign" from the root store. These root certificates have intermediates which have been revoked due to key compromise. A compromised key for a certificate authority can be used to issue certificates to enable MITM attacks. Upgrade to certifi 2026.10.19 and rebuild container images to refresh CA certificate stores.
Please see the links for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://github.com/certifi/python-certifi/security/advisories/GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2 * https://groups.google.com/a/mozilla.org/g/dev-security-policy/c/0R3XLJL6FuE/m/0XofdebrAAAJ
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-19445] Use-after-free of a server-side SSLContext when sni_callback switches contexts
item.description:
There is a CRITICAL severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
A remote, unauthenticated TLS client can make a server crash or call through a freed pointer if its sni_callback assigns a different context to SSLSocket.context (the documented way to select a certificate per server name) and nothing else keeps the original ssl.SSLContext alive. Typical cases are servers that create an SSLContext per connection or replace it while connections are open; servers that wrap their listening socket with it are not affected.
Mitigation: keep a reference to every SSLContext that sets sni_callback for the lifetime of the server. TLS clients are not affected.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-19445 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/158504
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-19553] SSLContext.wrap_bio() missing validation of server_hostname parameter
item.description:
There is a HIGH severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
`ssl.SSLContext.wrap_bio()` didn't require the `server_hostname` argument to not be `None` if `ssl.SSLContext.check_hostname` was set. Due to a missing parameter check in `SSLObject`, if the `server_hostname` argument isn't supplied then hostname verification would be silently skipped.
This defect could lead to programs where certificate hostname verification *appeared* to be succeeding with `SSLContext.check_hostname = True` and no `ValueError` being raised due to misconfiguration.
If the program passes a `server_hostname` value that isn't an empty string or `None` to any of these APIs then certificate hostname verification proceeds as expected and the program is not affected by this vulnerability.
Mitigating this vulnerability doesn't require updating Python or applying the patch. To mitigate, pass a valid non-`None` and non-empty `server_hostname` value to `SSLContext.wrap_bio()`, `asyncio.create_connection()`, or `asyncio.loop.start_tls()` and certificate hostname verification will proceed as expected. Upgrading to the latest version of Python or applying the patch only changes the behavior from silently skipping hostname verification to raising a `ValueError`, similar to `SSLContext.wrap_socket()`, when `server_hostname` isn't supplied.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-19553 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/158503
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-12345] Race condition in tempfile.TemporaryDirectory cleanup allows deleting files outside the temporary directory
item.description:
There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
The cleanup of tempfile.TemporaryDirectory is vulnerable to a race condition. An attacker who can modify the tree during cleanup can replace a directory with a symbolic link, causing files outside of the temporary directory to be deleted or have their permissions and file flags reset, with the privileges of the process performing the cleanup.
Note that platforms where shutil.rmtree.avoids_symlink_attacks is false, remain affected, and file flags may still be reset outside of the tree on all platforms.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-12345 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/157580
item.author: stanulbrych＠gmail.com (Stan Ulbrych)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-82049] tarfile extraction filters allow file modification and content disclosure via hard link to symlink
item.description:
There is a HIGH severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
In CPython 3.13 and earlier, the tarfile module's data and tar extraction filters are vulnerable to crafted archives containing a hard link to a symbolic link. Such archives may cause extraction to modify the permissions or modification time of a file outside the destination directory, or expose the contents of that file within the extracted tree.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-82049 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/157192
-- Stan Ulbrych (https://stan.ulbrych.org)
item.author: stanulbrych＠gmail.com (Stan Ulbrych)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-87910] tarfile hardlink fallback ignores custom extraction filter rejection via None
item.description:
There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
When tarfile extracts a link on a system that doesn't support links, it falls back to extracting a member from the archive. In this case, the filter function is run twice: once for the extracted member, and once with name set to the location of the link. For one of the calls, the return value was ignored. Instead, the member should be skipped if either call returns None.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-87910 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/157266
item.author: encukou＠gmail.com (Petr Viktorin)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-15310] Memory exhaustion in zipfile in bzip2/LZMA/Zstandard decompression
item.description:
There is a LOW severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
When decompressing crafted zip files using the bzip/LZMA/Zstandard compressions, Python could use an attacker-controlled size to pre-allocate memory, possibly resulting in memory exhaustion.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-15310 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/156003
item.author: encukou＠gmail.com (Petr Viktorin)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-19672] tarfile extraction filter bypass allows creation of directories outside the destination
item.description:
There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
The tarfile module's tar and data extraction filters created directories outside the destination for members whose name leaves the destination and returns to it, such as ../evil/../dest/sub/file. The containment check used the resolved path, but intermediate directories were created from the name as given.
Only empty directories are created outside the destination. Member contents are still extracted inside it. To return to the destination the member's name must contain the destination directory's own final component, so extraction into a secure randomised directory is not affected.
This affects POSIX platforms only. On Windows, .. components are collapsed before the path reaches the filesystem, so the directories outside the destination are never created.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-19672 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/156000
item.author: stanulbrych＠gmail.com (Stan Ulbrych)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-15806] urllib.request.HTTPPasswordMgr credentials for one URL scheme sent over another scheme
item.description:
There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
The HTTPPasswordMgr class in the urllib.request module, along with its subclasses HTTPPasswordMgrWithDefaultRealm and HTTPPasswordMgrWithPriorAuth, did not take the URL scheme into account when matching stored credentials against a requested URL. Credentials added for an https:// URL were also used for requests to the same host over http://, so an attacker able to redirect or downgrade a client to plain HTTP (for example, via an HTTPS-to-HTTP redirect or an on-path position) could capture credentials in cleartext. Credentials added for http:// URLs could likewise be sent over https://.
Credential matching is now scoped by URL scheme. Credentials registered with a URL that includes a scheme are only used for requests with the same scheme. Credentials registered with a bare authority (such as example.com or example.com:8080) continue to match any scheme, preserving compatibility with existing code, including proxy authentication.
Users who cannot upgrade immediately can mitigate by ensuring that applications never make plain http:// requests to hosts for which credentials are registered, for example by not following redirects to http:// URLs.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
- https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-15806 - https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/155696
item.author: kirill.bast＠gmail.com (Kirill Podoprigora)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-17084] StringPrep algorithm considered Unicode codepoint attributes outside Unicode 3.2.0
item.description:
There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
The "stringprep" module didn't process characters from RFC 3454 tables B.2 or B.3 correctly: the latest Unicode codepoint attributes were used instead of the specified Unicode 3.2.0. This behavior would cause mismatches when processing domain names using IDNA 2003 (the "idna" codec) and the in_table_b2() function of the "stringprep" module. This only affects domain names containing characters that were not previously registered or had their Unicode attributes such as case-folding behavior updated since Unicode 3.2.0.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-17084 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/155293
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-18503] Super-linear CPU usage for unbounded input to csv.Sniffer.sniff()
item.description:
There is a LOW severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
Attacker-controlled CSV samples can trigger super-linear regular-expression work during dialect sniffing and consume significant CPU when applications pass unbounded input to csv.Sniffer.sniff().
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-18503 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/153694
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-13346] pip absolute path traversal during download from malicious package indexes
item.description:
There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting pip.
pip would incorrectly handle doubly-encoded package URLs from indexes allowing for files to be installed to arbitrary locations on disk even when installing wheels.
This vulnerability requires downloading or installing a package from a malicious package index to succeed, malicious packages alone are not able to exploit this vulnerability. Note that this vulnerability only materially impacts users running `pip download` with the `--only-binary` option as installing source distributions from an untrusted index is already an unsafe operation that executes code during install time.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-13346 * https://github.com/pypa/pip/pull/14110
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.title: [Security-announce]CVE-2026-6879 Quadratic Behavior in xml.etree.ElementPath Index Predicates
item.description:
There is a LOW severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
`Element.findall()` and fully-consumed `Element.iterfind()` exhibit `O(n^2)` time complexity when using XPath index predicates (e.g. `[1]`, `[last()]`, `[last()-N]`) on XML documents with many same-tag siblings. `Element.find()` is only affected when the first match is near the end of the sibling list, such as with `[last()]` or `[last()-N]`; `.//item[1]` short-circuits after the first match.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-6879 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/152676
item.author: encukou＠gmail.com (Petr Viktorin)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-15308] Incremental HTMLParser allows CPU-exhaustion DoS via repeated unterminated markup declarations
item.description:
There is a HIGH severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
The incremental HTML parser (html.parser.HTMLParser) allows for CPU denial-of-service through repeated unterminated markup declarations when processing uncontrolled data.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-15308 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/153031
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-4360] Tarfile.extract doesn't fully respect filter parameter
item.description:
There is a LOW severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
In the Tarfile.extract function, the filter parameter is not passed properly called when extracting hardlinks. An affected system that extracts content from untrusted tar files could end up writing files with an unexpected uid/gid despite the user passing filter='data' to the extract function.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-4360 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/151988
item.author: encukou＠gmail.com (Petr Viktorin)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-11972] tarfile opened in streaming mode mishandles EOF
item.description:
There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
When using the "tarfile" module with a file opened in "streaming mode" (mode="r|") the tarfile module did not properly handle EOF, meaning an archive could be parsed in an infinite loop.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-11972 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/151982
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-0864] Configparser newline injection in write() method
item.description:
There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
When using the "configparser" module to write configuration files containing multi-line text values with carriage return characters (\r) the resulting file could be injected with unexpected keys and values if the attacker controls the written value.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-0864 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/143929
item.author: seth＠python.org (Seth Larson)

item.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-11940] tarfile extraction filter bypass allows escaping the destination directory
item.description:
There is a HIGH severity vulnerability affecting CPython.
tarfile.extractall() with the 'data' or 'tar' filter could be bypassed by a crafted archive where a hardlink references a symlink stored at a deeper name than the hardlink itself. The extraction fallback validated the symlink at it's archived location but recreated it at the hardlink's shallower path, letting a relative target the filter judged contained escape the destination directory. This allowed a malicious tar archive to create a symlink pointing outside the destination, enabling out-of-destination file reads or writes. This was an incomplete fix of CVE-2025-4330.
Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions:
* https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-11940 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/151559
item.author: stanulbrych＠gmail.com (Stan Ulbrych)
